name: the expanded state of disclosure and dialog elements is selectable
expected_behavior: `:open` selects exactly the `<details>` and `<dialog>` elements carrying the expanded state, on its own, narrowed by element type, and nested inside `:not()` / `:is()`; `[open]` keeps matching every element that merely carries the attribute.

name: state pseudo-classes that need a live viewer parse and select nothing
expected_behavior: `:autofill`, `:buffering`, `:fullscreen`, `:picture-in-picture`, `:popover-open`, `:seeking`, `:stalled` and `:volume-locked` compile, select nothing, and compose inside larger patterns; pseudo-class names that are not real CSS still raise `SelectorSyntaxError`.

name: a namespace map with a non-string prefix is refused up front
expected_behavior: Compiling with a namespace map whose keys include an int, bool, float, tuple or frozenset raises `TypeError`; non-string URIs still raise `TypeError`; all-string maps compile and select in both the dict and iterable-of-pairs forms.

name: dumping a compiled selector's structure always terminates
expected_behavior: Asking any compiled selector to print its structure terminates and emits a multi-line rendering that mentions the selector's own values, positional and attribute selectors included.

name: a bracket-unterminated attribute test with a long bare value is refused promptly
expected_behavior: Compiling an attribute test with no closing bracket and a long unquoted value raises `SelectorSyntaxError` in time proportional to the input length; well-formed attribute tests, including escaped attribute names and the `|=` / `!=` operators, are unchanged.

name: an attribute test with an unterminated quoted value is refused promptly
expected_behavior: Compiling an attribute test whose single- or double-quoted value is never closed raises `SelectorSyntaxError` in time proportional to the input length; properly quoted values, including long ones and ones holding the other quote character, are unchanged.

name: a pattern whose selector count is far above the ceiling is refused
expected_behavior: Compiling a pattern of tens of thousands of selectors raises `ValueError`, whether they are written at the top level, reached through `:is()`, or reached through a custom `:--name` alias; a few hundred selectors still compile and select.

name: An+B index arithmetic agrees with the CSS selector specification
expected_behavior: Every `An+B` form selects exactly the siblings whose 1-based index equals a*n + b for some integer n >= 0, including sequences that cross index 0, land only on the last sibling, or use a negative step; `odd`, a bare integer and other established forms are unchanged.

name: prefix, suffix and substring attribute tests with an empty operand select nothing
expected_behavior: `[attr^=""]`, `[attr$=""]` and `[attr*=""]` select nothing, with or without a case flag and when combined with other conditions; non-empty operands, `[attr]`, `[attr=""]` and `[attr~=""]` are unchanged.

name: the silenced state of audio and video elements is selectable
expected_behavior: `:muted` selects exactly the `<video>` and `<audio>` elements carrying the silenced state, on its own, narrowed by element type, and nested inside `:not()` / `:is()`; `[muted]` keeps matching every element that merely carries the attribute.

name: week-numbered range controls agree with how many weeks a year has
expected_behavior: A week value naming a week number its year does not have counts as no value at all, so the control reports `:in-range`; a year that genuinely runs to a fifty-third week still compares against the limits, and no control is reported in both range states.

name: padding inside a pattern costs time proportional to its length
expected_behavior: A descendant combinator written as tens of thousands of whitespace characters or thousands of comments compiles and selects promptly and resolves to the same selector as the single-space form; short and edge padding are unchanged.

name: scanning a long element name costs time proportional to its length
expected_behavior: An element name tens of thousands of characters long followed by an illegal character raises SelectorSyntaxError promptly, wherever in the pattern the name sits; long legal names still compile and select, and long class and id names stay prompt.
